machine: Apple M1 Max, 32 GB unified memory

change.before: Each transformer kernel created, committed, and synchronously waited on its own command buffer.
change.after: Each transformer block uses one command buffer and one compute encoder. Explicit buffer barriers separate dependent stages; independent Q/K/V, Q/K normalization, and MLP gate/projection dispatches remain barrier-free between peers.

direct_two_step_ab.scope: The same 256px fixture trajectory prefix, including prefill step 1 and cached step 2. Packed-file validation and Metal setup occur before the measured loop.
direct_two_step_ab.gpu_time_warning: The sequential A/B runs had a 218.36 ms GPU-time difference from normal frequency and thermal variation. Comparing wall minus GPU time isolates submission and CPU synchronization overhead more reliably than comparing raw wall totals.

interpretation: Block-level batching removes most synchronous submission overhead, but matrix multiplication remains the dominant steady-state cost. The first true end-to-end wall breakdown also exposes roughly 59.1 seconds between entering the transformer phase and starting its denoising loop, primarily packed-artifact validation and runtime setup; this is a larger next target than further command submission work.
limitations: Metal GPU timestamps and wall clocks measure different scopes and must not be subtracted across separate runs without accounting for frequency variation.
The packed artifact is intentionally revalidated on every command today, so process startup is much slower than the measured denoising loop alone.
Batching is currently per block, not per denoising step. The remaining loop overhead is below 1.4% of measured wall time, so broader batching is not the next dominant optimization.
